newsitem.title: UK: BA orders three more Boeing 757-200s.
newsitem.headline: BA orders three more Boeing 757-200s.

text.p: British Airways Plc said on Thursday that it had ordered three new Boeing 757-200 aircraft, powered by Rolls-Royce RB211-E4 engines.

The airline said the order was part of its plan to increasing the capacity of its short-haul services operating out of London's already congested Heathrow airport by increasing the average size of aircraft it uses there.

BA said that over the next two years the short-haul fleet at Heathrow would be reduced to three aircraft types -- B-767s, B-757s and Airbus Industrie A320s, with smaller B-737s being moved to other airports.
"These orders will allow us to simplify the fleet structure at Heathrow," chief executive Robert Ayling said in a statement on Thursday.

"With the number of short haul types based at Heathrow being reduced within the next two years, the airline will benefit from reduced engineering and staff costs and provide us with a more flexible fleet to meet the demands of the operation."
